benchmark_text: IPCC AR6 WG3 concludes that limiting warming to 1.5C requires deep emissions reductions across all sectors with global emissions peaking before 2025.
IPCC AR6 endorses comprehensive GHG emissions accounting and rapid reduction across direct and indirect (Scope 1-3) emissions consistent with 1.5C pathways.
IPCC AR6 endorses carbon pricing as a key economic instrument for emissions reduction. Effective carbon prices need to align with deep decarbonization pathways.
IPCC AR6 finds that rapid scaling of renewable electricity to >70% by 2050 is required for Paris-aligned pathways. Policy support for renewables is consistent with IPCC analysis.
IPCC AR6 finds that fossil fuel subsidies are inconsistent with Paris-aligned pathways and their phase-out yields significant emissions reductions.
The EU 2035 ICE phase-out requires zero-emission new passenger cars and light commercial vehicles from 2035. The IPCC supports rapid transport electrification as Paris-aligned.
The EU ETS phase 4 reform tightens the cap and extends to maritime and buildings. IPCC analysis supports tightening market-based instruments.
The EPA methane rule (40 CFR Part 60) requires substantial leak detection and repair. The IPCC identifies methane reductions as among the highest-priority near-term mitigation actions.
